decisions.reason: As a low-risk complement to the core flooring business, the cleaning soap likely meets at least modest aspiration levels and is worth retaining while the firm learns about repeat demand.
The maintenance oil extends the established care system for wooden floors and, with several variants, fits the firm's capabilities and customer relationships well enough to stay on the market.
Because it closely supports users of oiled wood floors already served by the firm, management would likely tolerate some early uncertainty and keep it unless results clearly fall below aspirations.

The moisture-protection underlay strengthens the firm's system offering for installers and project buyers, so it is likely to be kept unless early sales prove distinctly weak versus comparable accessories.

High-density underlay foam is somewhat more exposed to overlap and price competition than the care products, but its strategic fit with floor installation still makes retention more likely than withdrawal.

The oak parquet line is very close to the firm's established business, uses core know-how and channels, and would likely be kept as long as performance is near normal aspirations for new flooring lines.
